name: todo-vault-workspace
description: Local-first, Jira-shaped task vault, plus the desktop app over it

scripts.//test: The glob is load-bearing and needs Node 22. npm runs scripts through cmd.exe on Windows, which does not expand globs, so the pattern reaches Node's test runner intact — and expanding it there is a feature Node gained in 22. apps/desktop does the same. This is what the engines floor below is really about.
scripts.dev: npm run build -w todo-vault && npm run dev -w @todo-vault/desktop
scripts.//preview: Building core first is not optional: `start` alone assembles the desktop bundle around whatever packages/core/dist was left containing, which looks like a clean build while carrying a stale core. The sequence lives here rather than in the menu so it holds for anyone typing the command directly — a rule only the menu enforces is not enforced.
scripts.preview: npm run build -w todo-vault && npm run start -w @todo-vault/desktop

//engines: Was >=20, which nothing had ever tested and which was false: `npm test` globs its test files, and Node only expands those patterns from 22 on. Node 20 also left LTS on 2026-04-30, so the floor moved up to the oldest version that actually runs the suite rather than the suite retreating to the oldest version named here.
//allowScripts: npm 11.16+ blocks dependency install scripts until they are decided here (RFC npm/rfcs#868). esbuild's postinstall is denied rather than allowed: the binary arrives as the @esbuild/<platform> optional dependency, so esbuild loads, transforms and runs its CLI shim with the script blocked. Bare name rather than a pinned version, so a vite or electron-vite bump does not bring the warning back. Must stay in the ROOT package.json — npm ignores this field in a workspace.
